goal: Find the COVID-19 model to submit as ACCIDDA-Chromantis for reference date 7 November 2026 (Hub deadline Wednesday 4 November, 11 PM ET). Both targets, quantiles and 200 samples, horizons 0-3.
history: Restarts the COVID search of 14-15 October (covid-tree-20261014, covid-ed-20261015). All recipes are refit on the current code rather than reusing those fits. Those searches ended without acceptance because ED and national intervals looked too narrow, archive gaps were filled with finalized values, and prescribed-input and archived-input scores disagreed.
data: Frozen research panel data/processed/panel.npz, SHA256 b3cb41a0..., built 2026-10-05, finalized values as of 2026-09-22. Unchanged from the flu, RSV and October COVID searches, so the labels and Hub comparisons stay matched.
problem_in_words: COVID admissions and ED share, 1-4 weeks ahead. Each of 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 is held out in turn, training on the other seasons of 2022-23..2025-26. Labels are finalized future values.

evaluation_inputs.rule: Each season is scored on the most realistic inputs it has.
evaluation_inputs.2024-25 and 2025-26: Archived Wednesday reports (saved fits replayed, no refit). Finalized values fill archive gaps: of the newest reported week, 3% of admissions and 84% of ED values in 2024-25, and 14% of admissions and 19% of ED values in 2025-26.
evaluation_inputs.2023-24: Three shared artificial preliminary histories from the COVID 2025-26 reporting process, because no COVID report archive exists for that season (100% of archived inputs would be finalized fills, and the correction trees would then inflate already-final values).

selection_score: Primary: states/DC mean WIS of log(1 + admissions), October-May reference dates, horizons 0-3, seasons equal; lower is better. The ranking tables average each seed's own score over seeds; they are not mixtures (the text said mixture until 31 October, which was wrong). Real mixtures, as a release would be, are scored separately with chromantis.evaluation.ensembles and are lower because mixing helps. Finalists are compared on mixtures.
gates: Strict forward check on archived 2025-26 reports: trained on 2022-23..2024-25, artificial errors from the 2024-25 reporting process. A finalist must not be clearly worse here than the fallback.

ED natural-scale WIS relative to CovidHub-ensemble, states/DC and US separately, and US admissions, reported beside the primary score; an ED-weak admissions winner may be routed to a separate ED recipe.
Interval coverage at 50/80/90/95%, states/DC and US separately. Mixing is preferred where it repairs coverage; no calibration is fitted on evaluation outcomes.
Live check: the final release is replayed on the 14, 21 and 28 October and 4 November reports and scored against Hub models on observed weeks.

Live gate, added 31 October: every candidate is also judged as an all-season fit replayed on the 2026-27 reports, because leave-one-season-out scores do not measure an all-season fit. The evidence is thin and covers horizons 0-1 only until later truth arrives.
fallback: production/releases/covid-half-perturbation-candidate-20261015.json: equal mixture of a width-256 direct-quantile MLP and a width-192 sampled MLP, reporting errors on half the training episodes, ten seeds each, trained on 2022-23..2025-26. Frozen before the current reports. Replayed on 14 and 21 October reports with no refit, on the three observed horizon-tasks per state and DC (153 tasks, weeks ending 17 and 24 October), its mean WIS of log(1 + admissions) is 0.178 against 0.170 for CovidHub-ensemble and 0.368 for CovidHub-baseline, 5th of 15 models; lower is better. Its 95% interval covered 94% and its 50% interval 58%. ED share WIS is 0.77 times CovidHub-baseline against 0.73 for the ensemble. Two weeks of a slow decline say little.
assumptions: The frozen panel's truth (22 September) is close enough to final for training labels and retrospective scoring.
The 2025-26 reporting process approximates 2026-27 reporting. The strict forward check uses the 2024-25 process instead.
October-May is the relevant selection window for forecasts starting in November; June-September is inspected only for finalists.
Forecasts are made with 512 samples for scoring, as for every study.
expansion_rule: As rsv-tree-20261013: four seeds per node; a child counts as better than its parent only if lower by more than the pooled seed noise; the next round expands the best nodes and combines what helped. Final choice among seed and recipe mixtures.

execution.launcher: scripts/covid_tree.sbatch, one array over 4 L40 and 2 H100, 8 fitting lanes each; scripts/covid_tree_score.sbatch ranks and replays each finished stage

decisions: 2026-10-30: round 1 = 13 roots and 54 children (67 recipes, 4 seeds). Roots: half-perturbation and full-perturbation versions of the width-256 direct-quantile and width-192 sampled MLPs; width-256 trained on archived reports; width-512 trained on archived reports; Bes as the known over-correcting control; A_blocks3 from the flu B7 mixture; the best October architecture; and the four RSV recipes with COVID targets. Children change, on both half-perturbation roots: ED transform, a separate national head, correction strength and view, reporting-error share and strength, cross-pathogen inputs, calendar, lookback, recent-only training, log-count space, encoder, width and loss weight. Added for the sampled root: the strong-KL conditional VAE that helped flu forward in time, correction noise, and neighbouring-state exchange. Added for the quantile root: no exchange, regional attention, deeper decoder, and half archived reports. Correction strength is included because the live flu Bes forecast showed that too strong a correction over-forecasts.

2026-10-30 16:50 EDT: while round 1 fits. Applying the new per-season input rule to the October seeds 54-57 (trained on the other seasons of 2022-23..2025-26, finalized future labels) puts finalized-history recipes first: width-256 quantile MLP 0.2397, width-512 0.2405, against 0.2458 for the half-reporting-error version and 0.2486 for full errors; states/DC log-admission WIS, lower is better. The strict forward check on archived 2025-26 reports still has half-errors slightly ahead (0.2514 against 0.2554 for finalized). Round 1 has no finalized root, so before any worker reached it, reseed-01 was replanned to add finalized roots (width-256 quantile, width-192 sampled, width-512 quantile) on seeds 204-207, matched to the error-trained roots on those seeds. Added production-00: all-season fits of seven plausible recipes, queued after the search so the GPUs stay busy and a winner among them needs no wait.

2026-10-30 22:30 EDT: Bh.regionattn crashed on all four seeds in both round 1 and the forward check (the US locations file has no state_abb column, which regional attention reads). Because the launcher queued scoring only when every run was complete, those two stages sat fitted but unscored for about 1.5 hours. Regional attention is dropped rather than fixed, and both stages are scored with the other 66 recipes; the launcher now queues scoring once no run is left to fit. Fresh seeds 204-207 (trained on the other seasons of 2022-23..2025-26, finalized future labels, per-season input rule; states/DC log-admission WIS, lower is better): finalized-history width-256 quantile MLP 0.2406, archived-report-trained 0.2414, half-errors 0.2424, all within seed noise; full errors 0.2544 and width-192 sampled 0.2530 to 0.2618. Added forward-02: strict forward check of the three finalized recipes on seeds 200-203, matched to forward-01.

2026-10-31 12:20 EDT: round 1 scored (66 recipes, seeds 200-203). No clear winner: the same recipes shift by 0.010 between seed sets (errors on half of episodes scored 0.2526 on seeds 200-203 and 0.2424 on seeds 204-207), more than most gaps at the top. Round 1 tested almost no covariates (Kinsa only, inside two RSV recipes). Round 2 (60 recipes, seeds 200-203) adds inpatient claims, outpatient claims, wastewater level and rank, Kinsa and two pairs on the finalized quantile, 25%-error quantile and half-error sampled roots; other location-exchange designs, encoders and decoders; and combinations with the national head and weight decay. Forward-03 repeats it trained on 2022-23..2024-25 with the 2024-25 reporting process and reruns the finalized recipes, because forward-02 kept the 2025-26 reporting setting and its 0.2428 is not trusted. Decision: the GPUs were idle from 22:20 on 30 October to 12:15 on 31 October because the local check that should have woken me did not.

2026-10-31 12:55 EDT: asked to keep runs going for 24 hours. Chained in Slurm after round 2, its forward check and reseed-02, in this order: all-season fits of five round 1 leaders; round 3 (60 designs no COVID round has tried, such as other encoders, separate admissions and ED fits, autoencoders, other correction models and interval-related sampled options) and its forward check; 36 ED-only specialists and their forward check; 8 more seeds for 10 leaders and comparisons; rounds 2, 3 and the rest of round 1 on seeds 204-207 with forward checks; 16 further seeds for the leaders. Round 3 dropped three invalid combinations. About 3,150 runs remain, roughly 25 hours at round 1's speed of about 125 runs per hour. The tail is filler and may be replaced when results arrive.

2026-10-31 15:55 EDT: round 2 scored (60 recipes, seeds 200-203, trained on the other seasons of 2022-23..2025-26, finalized future labels, per-season input rule; states/DC log-admission WIS on the seed mixture, lower is better). Replacing exchange with neighbouring states by a whole-country summary is the first gain larger than the seed noise. The finalized-history width-256 quantile MLP scores 0.2394 with neighbouring-state exchange, 0.2244 with a state-mean plus US summary (spatial=pooled) and 0.2257 with a US-only summary (spatial=national_broadcast). All four seeds improve for both, and the strict forward check agrees (0.2541 against 0.2290 and 0.2355, trained on 2022-23..2024-25, scored on archived 2025-26 reports). The pooled version also largely removes the ED weakness: 2025-26 ED WIS relative to CovidHub-ensemble goes from 1.18 to 1.03 for states/DC and from 2.11 to 0.96 for the US. No covariate clearly helps: the best on the same root are wastewater 0.2358 and inpatient claims 0.2371-0.2375, within seed noise, and Kinsa is worse at 0.2502. US admissions 95% coverage remains 76%, too narrow. Pooled models were picked as the best of 60 on four seeds, so the gain may shrink. The array running round 3 was cancelled 20 minutes in (its unfinished runs return to the queue, finished ones stay) and resubmitted so that the next work is: all-season fits of six recipes; the best of round 2 and comparisons on fresh seeds 204-215 with forward check; round 4 (163 recipes with pooled exchange as the root) with forward check; 24 ED-only models with pooled exchange with forward check; then the previous queue in its previous order.

2026-10-31 17:50 EDT: confirmation and correction. Correction: scores in every earlier decision, including the 15:55 one that said 'on the seed mixture', are averages of per-seed scores, not mixtures. Correction: the 15:55 claim that pooled exchange largely removes the ED weakness came from four seeds; on fresh seeds it does not. On fresh seeds 204-215 (per-seed average, same training and inputs as the main score, lower is better) the 25%-error US-only quantile MLP scores 0.2296 main and 0.2334 forward, the finalized US-only 0.2282 and 0.2397, the finalized gated 0.2319 and 0.2388, the finalized state-mean plus US 0.2321 and 0.2464, against 0.2392 and 0.2514 for finalized neighbouring-state exchange. Real mixtures, seeds 204-215 (experiment covid-1030-mix01), trained and evaluated the same way: quantile-only US-only 25%-error + gated 0.2181 main and 0.2225 forward, ED ratio to CovidHub-ensemble 0.98 states/DC and 1.11 US; adding the sampled US-only model 0.2190 and 0.2247, ED 0.96 and 1.08, US admissions 95% coverage 84%, states/DC 96%. The fallback's design (half-error quantile plus half-error sampled, seeds 200-203 only) scores 0.2373 and 0.2374, ED 1.38 and 2.62. The export needs a sampled recipe to write the 200 samples, so the sampled model stays in. Two provisional releases written from all-season fits, seeds 42-51: covid-national-three-candidate-20261031 (25%-error US-only, gated, sampled US-only) and covid-national-four-candidate-20261031 (also finalized US-only). The search continues; these are not the final choice. Queue unchanged.

2026-10-31 18:15 EDT: live replay contradicts the retrospective ranking. Frozen all-season fits (trained on 2022-23..2025-26, seeds 42-51, finalized labels) replayed with no refit on the 14 and 21 October reports, 153 states/DC tasks on the weeks ending 17 and 24 October, mean WIS of log(1 + admissions), lower is better: CovidHub-ensemble 0.170, the 15 October fallback 0.178, covid-national-three 0.197, covid-national-four 0.197. Both new mixtures forecast too low (median sum 0.83 of observed), and their 31 October forecast falls to about 2,900 admissions in states/DC by horizon 3 against about 4,200 for the ensemble. The two provisional releases must not be submitted. Cause investigated: the forecast direction swings with the training seasons. Same recipes on the same reports: trained without 2025-26, median 1.11-1.26 of observed; without 2024-25, 1.01-1.12; without 2023-24, 0.90-1.00; on all four, 0.64-0.93 (states/DC median sum to observed). This is not specific to whole-country exchange: the finalized neighbouring-state recipe also swings, from 0.93 on all four to 1.22 without 2025-26, about as much as the US-only recipes, though the state-mean recipe swings most (0.64 to 1.19). The half-error neighbouring-state recipes were not tested on training subsets; fitted on all four seasons they are close to observed (Bh 0.98, Bh.ushead 0.99). Retrospective scores of leave-one-season-out fits never measured this, because an all-season fit is a different model. Mixing the three held-out-season fits gives 0.169 for the 25%-error US-only recipe and 0.172 with gated and sampled added; these were chosen after seeing the live weeks, on two correlated reference dates, so they are hypotheses. Queue reordered: all-season fits without calendar features and with weight decay (production-03); forward check with fewer training seasons so that averaging over training sets can be tested without live data (bag-forward-01, three subsets of 2022-23..2024-25, seeds 208-211); leaders-01; calendar check (cal-01); then the rest. Neighbouring-state mixtures are scored retrospectively in mix-02. The export crashes if a sampled recipe is listed after two quantile recipes in a three-recipe release, so the sampled recipe goes first.

2026-10-31 19:05 EDT: two explanations tested and neither supported. (1) Memorised seasonality: all-season fits without calendar features (seeds 42-51, same reports) are closer on observed weeks (US-only finalized 0.168 against 0.198, median/observed 0.98 against 0.86) but still fall steeply to horizon 3 (states/DC sum 2,762, against 4,172 for the ensemble), so calendar features are not the main cause of the decline. (2) Averaging over training sets: on the forward check (seeds 208-211, scored on archived 2025-26 reports) the 25%-error US-only recipe trained on all of 2022-23..2024-25 scores 0.2216, against 0.2450 for the mixture of three fits each trained on two of those seasons and 0.2349 with the full fit included; only the sampled recipe gains (0.2478 against 0.2423). This test uses two-season fits, while the live averages used three-season fits, so it is not a perfect match, but it gives no support to the averages that scored well live, which are dropped. Weight decay reduces the live too-low bias (US-only finalized 0.176, median/observed 0.98) and is scored retrospectively in round 4. Current lead: mixtures of the 25%-error US-only recipe with half-error neighbouring-state recipes, seeds 200-203 retrospectively and 42-51 live. With national head, weight decay and sampled US-only: main 0.2208, forward 0.2267, ED ratio 1.11 states/DC and 1.26 US, live 0.175 and US 0.050. With a sampled neighbouring-state model instead: main 0.2236, forward 0.2264, ED 1.15 and 1.45, live 0.172 and US 0.041. The fallback's design is main 0.2373, forward 0.2374, ED 1.38 and 2.62, and the frozen fallback 0.178 and US 0.048 live. These mixtures were picked after seeing the live weeks. They are confirmed next on seeds 208-215 (mix-03) once leaders-01 is scored.

2026-10-31 20:31 EDT: fresh-seed check of the leading mixtures (mix-03). Real mixtures of the seeds, no refit, seeds 208-215 (mix-02 used 200-203, so eight seeds now against four, and the seasons are the same). Main score: states/DC mean WIS of log(1 + admissions), trained on the other seasons of 2022-23..2025-26 with finalized future labels, evaluated on 2023-24 artificial histories and on archived 2024-25 and 2025-26 reports, lower is better. Forward check: trained on 2022-23..2024-25, evaluated on archived 2025-26 reports, lower is better. 25%-error US-only + half-error neighbouring-state weight-decay + half-error sampled neighbouring-state (pN+Wd+An): main 0.2236 (0.2235 on seeds 200-203), forward 0.2327 (0.2250), ED ratio to CovidHub-ensemble states/DC 1.09 (1.05), US 1.50 (1.39). Fallback design Bh+Ah on the same seeds: main 0.2371 (0.2373), forward 0.2451 (0.2374), ED 1.21 (1.38), US 1.71 (2.62). The gain over the fallback design holds on the main score and shrinks a little on the forward check, and ED ratios moved a lot between seed sets, so small ED differences are noise. Live replay: all-season fits, seeds 42-51, 14 and 21 October reports, observed weeks only (153 states/DC tasks, 3 US): pN+Wd+An 0.174 states/DC, 0.045 US; pN+U+Wd+An 0.172, 0.041; fallback 0.178, 0.048; CovidHub-ensemble 0.170, 0.048. Across states the 90% bootstrap interval of the difference from the fallback includes zero for every mixture, so the live weeks do not separate them. The retrospectively strongest options fail or weaken live: 25%-error US-only alone is main 0.2207, forward 0.2226 but live 0.187; pN+G+Ah.N is main 0.2196 but live 0.197 (do not submit); pN+Wd+Ah.N main 0.2222 but live 0.180. Decision: pN+Wd+An is the provisional candidate, preferred over pN+U+Wd+An because it is at least as good on every retrospective score on both seed sets, has one recipe fewer and its live deficit of 0.002 is well inside noise. It is not frozen: round 4 and its forward check may replace it, and it was chosen after seeing the live weeks. Calendar features stay: fits without them are worse retrospectively (seeds 204-207, seed averages, main score: US-only finalized 0.2514 against 0.2282 with calendar on seeds 204-215; 25%-error 0.2463 against 0.2296; gated 0.2686 against 0.2319; forward 0.2410 against 0.2397, 0.2404 against 0.2334, 0.2641 against 0.2388).

2026-11-03 10:24 EST: candidate chosen for the first submission (reference date 7 November): production/releases/covid-gru-four-candidate-20261103.json, an equal mixture of four recipes refit on all of 2022-23..2025-26 with finalized labels, seeds 42-51 each: the half-error sampled neighbouring-state recipe (Ah.neighbors), the 25%-error US-only recipe with a GRU encoder (pN.enc_gru), the finalized US-only recipe with multiscale features (N.multiscale), and the half-error neighbouring-state recipe with weight decay (Bh.wd). Retrospective, real mixtures of seeds 208-215 (mix-04), states/DC log(1 + admissions) WIS, lower is better: main score 0.2197 (the 31 October provisional pN+Wd+An 0.2236; fallback design Bh+Ah 0.2371); forward check trained 2022-23..2024-25 and scored on archived 2025-26 reports 0.2296 (0.2327; 0.2451); 2025-26 ED WIS ratio to CovidHub-ensemble states/DC 1.06 (1.09; 1.21), US 1.41 (1.50; 1.71); US admissions 95% coverage 89% (83%; 85%). Live replay of the frozen release on the 14 and 21 October reports, 153 states/DC and 3 US tasks, horizons 0-1, truth as of 28 October: log admissions WIS states/DC 0.172, US 0.039 (CovidHub-ensemble 0.170, 0.048; fallback release 0.178, 0.048); ED WIS x1e4 states/DC 3.92, US 1.83 (ensemble 3.88, 1.85; fallback 4.09, 2.99). 31 October forecast, states/DC median sum at horizon 3: 3,962 (ensemble 4,172; fallback 4,242). The GRU recipe was picked from 26 all-season recipes on these live weeks, and the four-recipe mixture was picked among 18 mixtures on the same seeds 208-215 that score it, so its margins over the close alternatives (Gru+Wd+An main 0.2223, Gru+pN+Wd+An 0.2202) are not established; its margin over the fallback design holds on every retrospective and live score. Round 4's retrospective leaders forecast far too low as all-season fits (state-mean exchange with log loss weight 1: main 0.2234 but live 0.258, median 0.70 of observed), so the live gate decided. Model loading fix: recipes with target-level exchange could not be reloaded (remote_groups, target_remote in saved settings); round 3 and 3b report scores now exist and none beats the leaders. Round 5 (GRU encoder on other roots and options) runs for next week; it does not change this release. The 4 November replay and the submission need the user's go-ahead.
